thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Gains 332 Points, Books Best Day In 3 Weeks As Apple Stock Surges To Record

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Gains 332 Points, Books Best Day In 3 Weeks As Apple Stock Surges To Record
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Buffett bet on Apple lifts broader market, supporting tech sector
U.S. stocks logged sharp gains Friday, with major indexes shaking off an early slide as technology stocks--notably Apple Inc.--rallied, overshadowing uncertainty over tense trade talks between the U.S. and China and a weaker-than-expected rise in April nonfarm payrolls.
What did the main benchmarks do?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 332.36 points, or 1.4%, to end at 24,262.51, recovering from an earlier drop of about 150 points. The blue-chip average logged its biggest daily climb since April 10, according to FactSet data. However, the average has struggled lately, falling in nine of the past 13 sessions.
The S&P 500 index rose 33.69 points, or 1.3%, to finish at 2,663.42. The Nasdaq Composite Index rose 121.47 points, or 1.7%, to close at 7,209.62, pushing the gauge back into positive territory for the week. All three indexes had opened lower.
Friday's gains were broad based, with all 11 S&P 500 sectors higher on the day. Tech was by far the biggest boost to markets, though, gaining 2%.
Friday's gains weren't enough to push the Dow and S&P into positive territory for the week, with both posting 0.2% weekly declines. The Nasdaq turned positive for the five-session stretch, however, up 1.3%.
What's driving markets?
Apple Inc.(AAPL) stock finished up 3.9%, boosting markets broadly after CNBC reported Berkshire Hathaway bought 75 million shares of the iPhone maker in the first quarter (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/warren-buffetts-berkshire-hathaway-bought-75-million-apple-shares-in-first-quarter-2018-05-03). The stock hit a record and was on track for its biggest weekly gain since October 2011.
Read:6 questions Warren Buffett should face at Berkshire Hathaway's annual meeting (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/6-questions-warren-buffett-should-face-at-berkshire-hathaways-annual-meeting-2018-05-04)
The U.S. created 164,000 new jobs in April, below the 188,000 that had been expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-164000-jobs-in-april-unemployment-falls-to-39-2018-05-04). Separately, the unemployment rate fell to 3.9% from 4.1%, the first time the jobless rate has dropped below 4% since the end of 2000.
In Beijing, U.S. and Chinese officials were meeting for discussions on tariffs and other trade issues. Worries about trade hostilities between the top two global economies have roiled financial markets in recent months.
Read:Here's how sensitive the stock market has become to 'trade war' talk (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-investors-are-overreacting-to-trade-war-threat-these-charts-say-2018-05-03)
The U.S. has handed China a lengthy list of demands, The Wall Street Journal reported, including a demand to reduce the bilateral trade deficit by at least $200 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-seeks-200-bln-cut-in-china-trade-imbalance-2018-05-04) by the end of 2020. The deficit stood at $375 billion last year.
What did Fed speakers say?
The central tendency of Federal Reserve officials in March was for three or four rate increases this year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/feds-williams-says-3-4-rate-hikes-this-year-is-still-right-way-to-think-about-policy-outlook-2018-05-04)and that is still the "right way to think about" the policy outlook in May, said San Francisco Fed President John Williams
New York Fed President William Dudley said Friday he's be surprised if there was a recession in the next two years. "I'd be surprised if the expansion would end in the next year or two," Dudley said in a discussion at Bloomberg headquarters in New York (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/feds-dudley-says-hed-be-surprised-if-recession-hits-in-next-two-years-2018-05-04).
Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Randal Quarles was set to speak at 5:30 p.m. Eastern.
Dallas Fed President Rob Kaplan, Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic and Kansas City Fed President Esther George are all slated to take part in a panel discussion at the conference at 8 p.m. Eastern.
What are strategists saying?
"Apple is releasing a lot of energy in tech shares today. It's obviously a big bode of confidence to have an investor like Buffett take such a big position, and the company just reported strong results, so there's a lot of goodwill around the stock," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at Wunderlich Securities.
"On top of that, we haven't had any negative surprises coming out of the trade talks, and there was as much good news as bad news in the jobs report, with the good news being no wage pressure to add to inflation fears, and an unemployment rate with a three-handle. It's really the best-case scenario."
Which stocks are in focus?
Newell Brands Inc. (NWL) rose 3.6% after first-quarter earnings beat forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/newell-brands-beats-profit-expectations-revenue-was-in-line-2018-05-04). The consumer-goods company also announced an agreement to sell packaging maker The Waddington Group for about $2.3 billion.
Alibaba (BABA) gained about 3.5% after the Chinese e-commerce giant posted fiscal fourth-quarter revenue and earnings that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alibaba-stock-gains-after-revenue-and-earnings-beat-expectations-2018-05-04).
Celgene Corp.(CELG) rose 1.7%. The biotech company posted first-quarter earnings ahead of forecast (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/celgene-shares-rise-on-q1-profit-revenue-beats-2018-05-04) and provided a 2018 outlook above analysts' expectations.
VF Corp. shares (VFC)fell 2.8% despite reporting an adjusted profit that was better than expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/vf-corp-earnings-beat-consensus-2018-05-04) and revenue growth of about 22%.
After the close, Berkshire Hathaway Inc.(BRKA) (BRKA) is scheduled to release its quarterly earnings report. Chief Executive and Chairman Warren Buffett hosts Berkshire's annual meeting on Saturday. The stock's Class B shares rose by 2.1%.
Check out: How Warren Buffett's stock picks for Berkshire Hathaway have performed in 2018 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-how-warren-buffetts-stock-picks-for-berkshire-hathaway-have-performed-in-2018-2018-05-03)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-how-warren-buffetts-stock-picks-for-berkshire-hathaway-have-performed-in-2018-2018-05-03)Pandora Media Inc.(P) shares soared about 20% after the streaming-music company late Thursday posted an earnings and revenue beat (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pandora-stock-rises-after-earnings-and-revenue-beat-2018-05-03).
CBS Corp.(CBSA) rose 8.8% after the media company late Thursday swung to a quarterly profit (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-swings-to-quarterly-profit-reports-sales-beat-shares-rise-2-2018-05-03) and reported a sales beat.
GoPro Inc.(GPRO) jumped 9.1% after the technology company late Thursday posted earnings that beat expectations.
Shake Shack Inc.(SHAK) shares jumped 18% a day after the burger chain posted an earnings beat and lifted its outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shake-shack-shares-jump-after-earnings-beat-outlook-raised-2018-05-03).
What are other markets doing?
European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-find-cheer-in-china-talks-but-french-banks-pull-back-2018-05-04) were trading higher, while Asian stocks closed mostly lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/all-quiet-in-asian-markets-ahead-of-us-jobs-report-2018-05-03).
Gold prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-lower-heads-for-1-weekly-loss-ahead-of-jobs-report-2018-05-04) settled down nearly 0.2% at $1,314.70 an ounce, and booked a weekly drop of about 0.7%, while U.S. oil futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-turns-higher-as-dollar-moves-looming-decision-on-iran-sanctions-tug-at-market-2018-05-04) surged on geopolitical news to end sharply higher. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index was up 0.2% at 92.539 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-springs-higher-as-us-jobs-data-take-center-stage-2018-05-04), marking a second weekly gain for greenback.
-- Barbara Kollmeyer and Sara Sjolin contributed to this article
